clue.text: With sun out, melon burst (not serious!)

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the word sun are rearranged on their own
a burst melon is broken apart, so its letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A melon splits open in the hot sun, a comic, not very solemn scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word has its own anagram signal: 'out' rearranges sun to UNS and 'burst' rearranges melon to OLEMN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking gravity or ceremony is unserious, which the prefixed word for 'not grave' expresses.

clue.text: When I start to speak, it's well old-fashioned!

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase places a moment upon the uttering of a word
a dated exclamation of surprise, like 'well!' or 'goodness!'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that starting a sentence with this sort of interjection sounds very dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated exclamation of surprise, and taken literally means at the point of speaking.

clue.text: Recycled scrap, then, retaining temperature in the toilet U-bend?

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside, so the abbreviation goes within the rearranged letters
recycled suggests the letters are reprocessed into a new order

explanation.surface: Recycled rubbish keeps warm inside the plumbing beneath a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The query on 'toilet U-bend?' marks it as an example: a U-bend is one kind of the trap the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-bend holds water to block foul smells rising from drains, which is what this plumbing trap is for; the query marks it as an example.

clue.text: Following dead right

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: A three-word phrase about pursuing someone and being dead right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes after or subsequent to another happens at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Awkward, harsh-hearted wedding officiator gets the bird

indicators.note: hearted means put at the heart, so the scrambled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: one who marries a couple is a marrier

indicators.note: awkward implies clumsily arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted registrar is given the bird, booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being jeered off stage, but 'the bird' is the definition; 'Awkward' rearranges harsh to ARSHH, and 'hearted' sets it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: This raptor is a bird of prey that hunts low over wetlands and reed beds.

clue.text: Dudley's famous role: showing paintings etc by Ben?

parts.note: paintings and the like are art
Ben suggests Ben-Hur, the film, so the word that follows Ben in that title is supplied

explanation.surface: A gallery shows paintings, apparently by somebody named Ben, tied to a comedian's famous part.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley Moore played the drunken millionaire in the 1981 film of this name; the question mark flags that Ben stands for what follows it in 'Ben-Hur'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudley Moore's best-known film character was the title playboy in the comedy of that name.

clue.text: Tiny pigs swallowing coin, nuts and bolts

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so the coin goes within

parts.note: runts are the smallest piglets of a litter
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Little piggies gobble a coin along with assorted hardware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts and bolts' looks like hardware for the pigs to eat, but is the idiom for the basics.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuts and bolts of a subject is an idiom for its basic elements or fundamentals.

clue.text: See 19
John Moor gets up after the others

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the other one

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: in a down clue, gets up means the word reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A man called John Moor rises later than everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a forename but is US slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: John is American slang for a lavatory, which is also called a washroom or a restroom.

clue.text: Open container for tip

parts.note: open, as in done in plain view, means overt
an urn is a container, as for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: An open container is suggested as a place for leaving a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' reads as a gratuity going into the jar, but it is the verb meaning to upset or knock over.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip a thing over is to upset or capsize it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: One lives without function as a handsome youth

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the other pieces stand around the word for function

parts.note: an, the indefinite article, means one
a do is a social function or party
lives, in the sense of exists, is the verb is

explanation.surface: Someone lives without any purpose, like a pretty but idle young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is read in its archaic sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name stands for any good-looking young man.

clue.text: Administrative departments giving head of Channel 4 and 1 Live employment

indicators.note: head of means only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
I is one in Roman numerals
L marks the live terminal on a British electric plug
service is employment, as in being in someone's service

explanation.surface: Broadcasters' bosses at Channel 4 and BBC Radio 5 Live set government jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: A British plug's three terminals are marked L (live), N (neutral) and E (earth).
explanation.definitionFit: The government departments staffed by permanent officials together form the state's administrative service.

clue.text: Mismatch? Cry out "That's what 5 26's 20 is really about!"

indicators.note: cry out read as cry put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a play about witches is really an allegory of political persecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 26's 20 is Arthur Miller's The Crucible, written as an allegory of the 1950s anti-communist witch hunts in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible used the Salem trials to depict Senator McCarthy's anti-communist hunts, which bear his name as a term for such campaigns.

clue.text: Shrill, it mutated with TB — tragic end to pregnancy

indicators.note: mutated means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrill cry and a mutated tuberculosis germ end a pregnancy tragically.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby born dead after the twentieth week is the sad outcome of a pregnancy, matching the definition.

clue.text: One complaining about Mr E. coming to a death

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a griper is one who complains
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whinger fusses about Mr E. coming to a fatal end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' is a link joining Mr E. to 'a'; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooded skeleton with a scythe personifies death in folklore.

clue.text: See 19
Uncertainty at Chinese transformation

indicators.note: a transformation is a change of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doubts arise over a Chinese makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is indecision or doubt, a near synonym of uncertainty.

clue.text: Odd rationale for one losing the sympathy of others

definitions.text: one losing the sympathy of others

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange or irregular, so the following word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange line of reasoning puts off everyone who hears it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estranges or turns others away is by definition one who alienates them.

clue.text: Returning prophet trapping nit by old city is a comfort

indicators.note: trapping means holding something within, so the other pieces go inside
returning means the word for prophet is read backwards

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
a nit is a fool, as is an ass
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: A prophet comes home holding an idiot and an ancient town, which somehow comforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses the prophet to REES before 'trapping' puts the fool and the city inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to comfort them, so the verb in the third person equals 'is a comfort'.

clue.text: Males turned intellect against church — meet subject matter for 5 26's 20

indicators.note: against means next to, so one piece is set right beside the other
turned means the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: wit is intelligence or intellect
a meet is a gathering for a hunt, so it stands for a hunt

explanation.surface: Men turn their minds against the church and gather, as in a Puritan drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 26's 20 is Arthur Miller's The Crucible, which dramatises the 1692 Massachusetts witch trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Miller's play is set during the 1692 Massachusetts trials of accused sorcerers, its whole plot.

clue.text: Electric Hub variety theatre

indicators.note: variety implies a different mix, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A music-hall venue named the Electric Hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety theatre' looks like a music-hall phrase, but 'variety' is the anagram signal and 'theatre' alone means a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is Arthur Miller's 1953 stage play, and theatre can mean drama or a stage work.

clue.text: Poison injector produced by horse artist

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A venom-delivering creature produced by a horse painter.
explanation.definitionFit: This snake delivers venom through its fangs, so it injects poison when it bites.

clue.text: See 8
In hindsight, m'lud, it helps make web pages

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lawyer says, looking back, that something helps build websites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hindsight' looks like a stock phrase but 'In' signals the letters at the end of hindsight and start of m'lud.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypertext Markup Language is the coding standard used to build web pages.

clue.text: 75% of talent seeking is spin

indicators.note: 75% of an eight-letter word keeps six letters, here the closing three quarters

parts.note: searching for talent, as football clubs do, is scouting

explanation.surface: Most of a talent hunt is just hype or media spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' looks like PR spin but means a short trip out; dropping the first two of eight letters leaves three quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short drive or jaunt, the same as a little excursion or trip.

clue.text: Member, honourable, getting backing — prepare for activity

parts.note: a limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body

indicators.note: getting backing means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: pure, morally unsullied, means honourable

explanation.surface: An honourable MP gets support before getting ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member, honourable' suggests a Parliamentary honourable member; in fact LIMB is followed by PURE reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen the muscles before exercise is a phrasal verb meaning to get ready for physical activity.

clue.text: One involved in daily grind gets married (even worse afterwards)

indicators.note: afterwards says this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: iller, more ill, means even worse

explanation.surface: A worker stuck in the daily grind marries and ends up feeling worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily grind' is the cliché for routine work, but a flour-maker literally grinds daily; also 5 26 is the playwright Arthur Miller.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller grinds corn into flour every day, making the phrase a literal job description.

clue.text: Came upon a local alternative for what 5 26's 20 was for 12?

parts.note: came upon means met, as in encountered
a local is a pub, a public house, abbreviated PH
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone found a pub alternative, and asked what a play was standing in for.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible uses the Salem witch trials as a figure for McCarthy's hunts of the 1950s. A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Miller's play stands for the anti-communist campaign figuratively, a figure of speech representing something else.
